newsitem.title: UK: Dalgety climbs after results impress.
newsitem.headline: Dalgety climbs after results impress.

text.p: Shares in food and agribusiness group Dalgety Plc rose on Monday after the company posted results toward the upper end of expectations, traders said.
Shares stood 11p higher at 338p by 0820 GMT.

The company said pretax profits in the year to June 30 excluding exceptionals were 101.9 million stg, down from 127.1 million stg in the previous year. Analysts had been forecasting a figure in the range of 90.0 million to 104.0 million stg.
Profits including exceptionals fell to 89.6 million stg, compared with 93.7 million stg in the previous year.
The company blamed hikes in raw material costs and the mad cow disease crisis for the drop in profits.
"The market was prepared for dismal results and the company said some encouraging things about the outlook," said David Lang, food analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.
Richard Clothier, Dalgety chief executive, said the overall result did not reflect the considerable progress the group had made during the year.
"Subject to the uncertain effect of BSE on Petfood exports and cattle feed, I remain confident of improved growth," he said in a statement accompanying the results.
